newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS-Richter boosts market share in H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Richter boosts market share in H1.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Vegyeszeti Gyar Rt boosted its domestic market share in the first half of 1997, the company's CEO Erik Bogsch told a news conference on Thursday.
"This was the first half-year...when Richter got the first ranking on the Hungarian market in terms of market share," he said.
"I would like to emphasise that the fact that we managed to boost our market share is important and not that we are in first place," he added.
Richter's domestic market share increased to 10.7 percent in the first half of the year from 9.8 percent in the first six months of 1996, Bogsch said.
Bogsch added the market share of domestic pharmaceuticals producers continued to narrow and fell by 1.5 percentage points to 42 percent.
"Foreigners boosted their volume sales by 15 percent, while domestic (producers) registered a nine percent fall," he said. "As a result total sales volume...fell by four percent in Hungary."

Richter released its first half IAS earnings report on Thursday and reported its net profit rising to 9.507 billion forints ($48.4 million) on sales of 24.837 billion from a net profit of 6.527 billion on sales of 18.070 billion in the first half of 1996.
Richter shares and Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) surged to new record levels both in Budapest and London, respectively, although profit-taking trimmed early gains on both markets.
In London, where trading starts earlier than in Budapest, Richter surged to a new high of $99.5 and at 0914 GMT it was marked at $97.75, up $1.6250.
In Budapest, Richter surged to a new high of 19,700 forints but came down and at 1031 GMT traded at 19,165 forints, up 365.
Within total revenues, the company's sales in Hungary rose to 7.512 billion forints from 6.071 billion, despite the fact that the health expenditure budget continued to impact volumes generally.
Bogsch said the company had launched four products in the domestic market, an agent to bring down blood pressure, two oral contraceptives and one treatment for ulcers.

Richter's exports amounted to $98 million for the January-June period, an increase of $14.6 million or 17.5 percent over the same six months of 1996 attributed primarily to strong demand from the CIS countries.

"Years of work we invested in the CIS markets to build a (distribution) network, and decades of work to make Richter's products well recognised, are behind the result," Bogsch said, adding that power of purchase has also grown on these markets.
The company benefited from the strong dollar, which helped its operating margins rise to 31.2 percent in the first half of 1997, compared with 28.9 percent for the same period in 1996.
"Margins benefited from the continuing strength of the U.S. dollar, primarily as the majority of exports are invoiced in U.S. dollars," Richter said in its earnings report.
The company added that while most exports were invoiced in U.S. dollars, operating expenses were incurred primarily in Hungarian forints.
-- Emese Bartha, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327-4040 ($ = 196.2 Hungarian Forints)
